_comment_family: Korolev is a family and this file is its Bold, but unlike the two
Telegraf cuts and the two Raleway ones it needs no care taken over
the name: the file already carries 'Korolev Bold' as name ID 1, keeps
the bare 'Korolev' in the typographic family (ID 16) with the cut in
ID 17, and repeats 'Korolev Bold' as the full name (ID 4). The family
name and the full name are the same string, so the name declared here
is both, and it answers with one cut whichever of the two a browser
That is the property those packs go to some trouble to buy, and it
is worth having for their reason even though nothing threatens it
today. One cut of Korolev is in fonts/ and one channel is set in it,
so there is nothing a bare family name could wrongly answer with -
until the day a Regular arrives beside it, which is a day this face
should not have to be rewritten for.
Weight 700, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. Stated rather than left to 'bold' so that the fallbacks below
resolve to a bold of their own family rather than to whatever the
browser picks when it is asked for nothing in particular.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the Windows full name (name ID 4) and the second the
PostScript name (ID 6); both name this one cut rather than a family
with cuts in it, so a machine answering to either is answering with
The first is also the name the installer registers the face under -
it copies each pack's font into the user's font folder and keys it by
local[0] (see engine.install_fonts), and Windows keys installed fonts
by their full name. So this list being in this order is what makes
the installed copy findable by the stack below.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied, and here they were
chosen by measuring, because the channel set in this face draws its
captions with no card under them and re-wraps nothing: a substitute
wider than the face the lines were broken against does not make a
different-looking caption, it makes one that runs out of the frame.
Korolev Bold is narrow for its weight. Its capitals average 0.552em,
and twenty of them - one caption line at the Snapchat preset's 20
characters - come out around 389px of the 486px a line has. What the
machine can be relied on to have measures, at the same size: Impact
361px, Segoe UI Bold 474px, Arial Bold 491px, Arial Black 551px. Only
the first of those leaves the line where it was.
So Impact first, which is the opposite of the reasoning in
telegraf-ultralight and lands here for the same underlying rule. That
face rejected Impact because a 200-weight hairline behind a heavy
condensed grotesque is the furthest possible thing from it; this one
is a heavy display cut itself, and the resemblance - metric first,
and visual only in so far as both are bold sans capitals - is as
close as a Windows machine gets. Segoe UI behind it at the declared
700, then Arial, each a little wider than the last and each a
caption that has lost a word off the end of a line rather than a
caption that has lost its face entirely.
Arial Black is absent, alone among the display faces in this folder.
At 42% wider than what the lines were measured against it is not a
fallback, it is a guarantee of overflow.
